q: Muscle cells of trained endurance athletes contain more mitochondria with more densely packed cristae. Which is the best explanation?
options: More cristae allow the muscle cells to carry out glycolysis at a much faster rate than before
More inner membrane means more oxidative phosphorylation – more aerobic ATP, less lactate
Cristae store extra oxygen, which the muscle can use when breathing can't keep up with demand
More mitochondria reduce the amount of ATP that muscle contraction requires
explanation: Aerobic training increases mitochondrial number and cristae area – more ETCs and ATP synthases, and more matrix enzymes for the link reaction and Krebs cycle – so more ATP comes from aerobic respiration and the lactate threshold rises. Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm, and O2 is stored by myoglobin, not by cristae.
